# sitegen

Static site generator for a small blog. Builds `content/` Markdown into `out/` HTML.

## Layout

- `content/posts/*.md` -- blog posts (front-matter: title, date)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` -- top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` -- shared template with `{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}` placeholders
- `static/style.css` -- shared stylesheet
- `build.py` -- build script (stdlib only)
- `tests/test_build.py` -- unit tests

## Build & test

    python3 build.py
    python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v

## Key behavior

- Posts go to `out/posts/<slug>.html`; top-level pages to `out/<slug>.html`
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Markdown subset: headings (#, ##, ###), paragraphs, links, **bold**

# sitegen

A small static site generator for a blog. Reads `content/` Markdown and builds a browsable site under `out/`.

## Quick start

```bash
python3 build.py          # build site -> out/
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests   # run tests
```

## Writing a post

1. Create `content/posts/my-post.md`:

```markdown
---
title: My Post Title
date: 2026-09-18
---

# My Post Title

Write in Markdown. Supports `#`/`##`/`###` headings, paragraphs, [links](https://example.com), and **bold**.
```

2. Run `python3 build.py`
3. Your post appears on the index automatically, sorted newest-first by date.

## Project layout

- `content/posts/*.md` — blog posts (front-matter: `title`, `date`)
- `content/index.md`, `content/about.md` — top-level pages
- `templates/page.html` — shared template (`{{title}}`, `{{nav}}`, `{{stylesheet}}`, `{{content}}`)
- `static/style.css` — shared stylesheet
- `build.py` — build script (stdlib only, no dependencies)
- `tests/test_build.py` — unit tests

## Output

- Posts → `out/posts/<slug>.html`
- Top-level pages → `out/<slug>.html`
- Index lists all posts sorted by date (newest first)
- Nav and stylesheet links use relative prefixes (posts use `../`)

Here's what I found and fixed:

**Bug: post pages had broken links.** The template hardcoded `style.css` and `index.html` paths, but posts live in `/posts/`, so those resolved to `/posts/style.css` — which doesn't exist. No stylesheet, no working nav.

**Fixes applied:**

1. **`build.py`** — `nav_html()` and `render_page()` now take a `prefix` argument. Posts pass `prefix="../"`, so nav links and stylesheet resolve to `../index.html`, `../style.css`, etc. Top-level pages use the default empty prefix.

2. **`templates/page.html`** — stylesheet href now uses `{{stylesheet}}` placeholder instead of hardcoding `style.css`.

3. **`tests/test_build.py`** — added `test_all_links_are_valid` which parses every `<a>` and `<link>` in the built output and asserts each href resolves to a real file. This catches regressions automatically.

4. **`README.md`** — rewrote for your colleague: quick start, how to write a post, project layout, and output structure.

**Verification:**
- `python3 build.py` → builds 3 posts + 2 pages
- All 6 tests pass, including the new link-checker test
- Confirmed post pages now have `../style.css`, `../index.html`, `../about.html`
